# Answer

## The scene

The moment in question runs from roughly **418 s to 426 s** of the video (burn-in timecode about **00:06:58 to 00:07:05**), in the shot that lasts 417.9–436.3 s. It is a Pride march through La Courneuve, in the Paris suburbs, and the march is moving along a tramway/boulevard — tram rails and a fenced tram platform are visible in the road behind the action.

The "mobile cart" is a **street vendor's improvised mobile market stall**: a wheeled table on casters with four thin metal corner poles, two parasols (red/yellow and black) fixed overhead, a large rainbow flag and a purple/blue flag draped over the front and sides, and its whole tabletop covered with loose merchandise — rainbow badges, beaded bracelets, cellophane packets, and, most relevantly, **bundles of small hand-held rainbow flags mounted on thin white plastic sticks**.

Three people are working the cart. A **woman dressed entirely in black** (auburn hair pulled into a bun, bracelet on her wrist) is at the rear/camera-right side, moving the cart along; she is clearly seen pushing it from behind later in the same shot (≈430–434 s). A **woman in a brown-plaid jacket with long dark hair** is at the front-left corner, gripping the corner pole with her raised hand and guiding that end of the cart. A **man in a white T-shirt** walks alongside.

At about **423 s (00:07:03)** the woman in black stops, stretches her arm out across the table and **points down toward the cart's front-left corner**. About a second and a half later, at **424.4–425.2 s**, the woman in the plaid jacket bends down at exactly that spot and the vendor reaches down too, to pick things up off the roadway.

## What causes the mini flags to fall off the cart

**The mini flags fall off simply because they are loose, unsecured stock lying in a heap right on the open, rim-less front edge of the moving cart's tabletop, and they are slid and swept over that edge by the movement of the cart and by the large rainbow flag lying across them.** Nothing dramatic happens: nobody knocks the flags off on purpose, there is no collision with another cart or person, and no vehicle hits the stall. Stated point by point, the chain of causes visible on screen is:

1. **The mini flags are never fastened or contained.** Frame-by-frame close-ups of the tabletop at 421–424 s show ten or more of the little rainbow flags simply fanned out loose on the table surface, not in a box, tub, bucket or rack. Several of their thin white sticks already project out past the front edge of the table before anything happens.

2. **The table has no lip, rail or edging on that side.** The top is a flat board with a cloth/flag draped over it, so there is nothing at all to stop items sliding off the front-left corner — the merchandise is held in place only by friction.

3. **The cart is being wheeled along the street while loaded.** It rolls on small casters over patched, cambered asphalt beside a kerb and over tram rails, so it vibrates, rocks and lurches as it is pushed. In the 25 fps close-ups of that corner across 422.0–422.5 s, the whole pile of little flags visibly shifts and slews forward-left in unison, with motion blur — the classic signature of the cart jolting and its unsecured contents sliding.

4. **A large rainbow flag lies on top of the mini-flag pile and drags across it.** A big rainbow flag is heaped over that front-left corner of the table, and a second large rainbow flag — worn as a cape by a marcher standing right at the cart's front-left corner — sweeps in from the left across the same corner between about 421.9 s and 422.5 s. As this large fabric slides and flaps over the pile, it catches the little flags and pushes them along with it toward the open edge.

5. **A stiff wind is blowing throughout the shot.** Crops of the top of the cart show every flag on the corner poles and around the parasols being whipped out horizontally and curled over. The same wind flaps the big rainbow flag draped across that front corner back and forth over the pile, which both nudges the little flags and helps carry the lightest of them off.

6. **The result is that the little flags are pushed and shaken over the unprotected front-left lip of the table and drop onto the road.** Comparing the same crop at 421.4 s and at 423.4 s, the dense fan of roughly ten white flag sticks at that corner has been reduced to only three or four scattered ones — the rest have gone over the side. This is why the woman in black points there, and why the woman at the front immediately stoops to that spot to gather them up.
